questions.question: If two cars travel the exact same distance of 10 miles, but Car A travels at a higher speed than Car B, how does Car A's travel time compare to Car B's?
options: Both cars take the same amount of time.
Car A takes a shorter time.
Car A takes a longer time.
Car A's time is always double Car B's time.

questions.question: If two runners jog for exactly 30 minutes, but Runner X has a greater speed than Runner Y, what can be concluded about the distance they covered?
options: Runner Y travels a greater distance in that time.
Both runners travel the exact same distance.
Runner X travels a greater distance in that time.
Speed does not affect the distance traveled in a fixed time.

questions.question: Which of the following formulas is used to calculate the speed of a moving object?
options: Speed = distance × time
Speed = time ÷ distance
Speed = distance ÷ time
Speed = force ÷ distance

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct set of units used to measure speed?
options: m/s, km/h, miles/h
m/s², kg, Newtons
metres, kilometres, miles
seconds, hours, minutes

questions.question: On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line (greater gradient) represent?
options: An object moving backwards at a constant slow pace
A faster movement
A slower movement
An object that has stopped moving

questions.question: When an object falls through the air, it eventually reaches a constant speed called terminal velocity. Under what condition does this happen?
options: When gravitational force becomes zero
When there is no air resistance acting on the object
When drag force is twice the gravitational force
When the drag and gravitational forces are equal

questions.question: How does increasing the surface area of a parachute affect the drag force acting on it?
options: It decreases the drag force.
It increases the drag force.
It has no effect on the drag force.
It makes the drag force drop to zero.

questions.question: A skydiver has reached their top speed (terminal velocity) while falling with an open parachute. How does the drag force compare to the force of gravity?
options: The drag force is the same size as the force of gravity.
The drag force is much larger than the force of gravity.
The force of gravity is much larger than the drag force.
Both forces have dropped to zero.

questions.question: What does a flat, level horizontal line represent on a distance-time graph?
options: An object moving at a constant high speed
A stationary object that is not moving
An object that is accelerating rapidly
An object returning to its starting position

questions.question: On a distance-time graph, what do upward and downward sloping lines indicate?
options: Movement in opposite directions
Movement at the exact same constant speed
The object is speeding up in both cases
The object has stopped moving

questions.question: What is the main reason for taking repeat readings during an experiment in science?
options: To change the independent variable automatically
To guarantee that no anomalies will ever occur
To reduce the effect of random errors
To make the experiment take longer to complete

questions.question: What should you do with an anomalous reading when calculating the average of your experimental results?
options: Exclude it and do not use it in calculations of averages.
Include it and treat it with double the weight of other values.
Add it only if it makes the average higher.
Replace all other readings with the anomalous value.

questions.question: In which direction does the force of friction always act on a moving object?
options: In the same direction as the movement
Directly downwards towards the center of the Earth
Perpendicularly upwards from the surface
Against the direction of movement

questions.question: According to the laws of motion, what will happen to an object moving at a steady speed in a straight line if there is no resultant force acting on it?
options: It will continue to move at a steady speed in a straight line.
It will immediately slow down and come to a complete stop.
It will begin to accelerate rapidly.
It will veer off into a circular path.

questions.question: What is the primary physical benefit of streamlining an object, such as a vehicle?
options: It increases gravitational pull.
It reduces drag.
It increases the weight of the vehicle.
It eliminates friction entirely.

questions.question: Why does streamlining reduce the drag force on an object moving through a fluid?
options: It increases the surface area exposed to the fluid.
It decreases the gravitational pull on the object.
It reduces how much fluid needs to be pushed out of the way.
It causes the fluid to become completely solid.

questions.question: As an object moves faster and faster through a fluid (such as water or air), what happens to the drag force acting on it?
options: The drag force remains completely constant.
The drag force decreases with speed.
The drag force increases with speed.
The drag force drops instantly to zero.
